claim: eIF3 is composed of 13 subunits in humans.
source: In humans, eIF3 is composed of 13 subunits and helps position ribosomes at the start codon of mRNAs (Jackson et al., 2010; Figure 1A).
evidence: Cited from Jackson et al., 2010

claim: eIF3 helps position ribosomes at the start codon of mRNAs.
source: In humans, eIF3 is composed of 13 subunits and helps position ribosomes at the start codon of mRNAs (Jackson et al., 2010; Figure 1A).
evidence: Cited from Jackson et al., 2010

claim: PAR-CLIP experiments in HEK 293T cells uncovered regulatory roles of eIF3 in the translation of a specific pool of mRNAs.
source: For instance, photoactivatable ribonucleoside-enhanced crosslinking and immunoprecipitation (PAR-CLIP) experiments (Hafner et al., 2010) performed in human embryonic kidney (HEK) 293T cells uncovered regulatory roles of eIF3 in the translation of a specific pool of mRNAs (Lee et al., 2015).
evidence: Cited from Lee et al., 2015

claim: EIF3D activates the translation of JUN mRNA by binding to its 5' cap.
source: These studies also revealed that eIF3 subunit d (EIF3D) activates the translation of JUN mRNA by binding to its 5' cap (Lee et al., 2016).
evidence: Cited from Lee et al., 2016

claim: The pool of mRNAs regulated by eIF3 varies dramatically across different cell types and physiological conditions.
source: Intriguingly, the pool of mRNAs regulated by eIF3 varies dramatically across different cell types and physiological conditions.
evidence: Inferred from comparison of different studies in different cell types mentioned in the text

claim: Robust T cell activation requires the direct interaction of eIF3 with the mRNAs encoding for the human T cell receptor subunits α and β.
source: PAR-CLIP experiments performed in Jurkat T cells showed that robust T cell activation requires the direct interaction of eIF3 with the mRNAs encoding for the human T cell receptor subunits α and β, a phenomenon that was also observed in primary T cells (De Silva et al., 2021).
evidence: Cited from De Silva et al., 2021

claim: eIF3 modulates the translation of mRNAs critical for adaptation and survival under stress conditions such as nutrient deprivation.
source: Additionally, eIF3 modulates the translation of mRNAs critical for adaptation and survival under stress conditions such as nutrient deprivation (Lamper et al., 2020).
evidence: Cited from Lamper et al., 2020

claim: eIF3 has been shown to be involved in translation elongation.
source: Beyond its established functions in translation initiation, eIF3 has been shown to also be involved in translation elongation (Lin et al., 2020; Wagner et al., 2020) and termination (Beznosková et al., 2013; Valásek, 2012; Valášek et al., 2017).
evidence: Cited from Lin et al., 2020 and Wagner et al., 2020

claim: eIF3 has been shown to be involved in translation termination.
source: Beyond its established functions in translation initiation, eIF3 has been shown to also be involved in translation elongation (Lin et al., 2020; Wagner et al., 2020) and termination (Beznosková et al., 2013; Valásek, 2012; Valášek et al., 2017).
evidence: Cited from Beznosková et al., 2013; Valásek, 2012; Valášek et al., 2017

claim: NPCs are considered more committed to the neural lineage than NSCs.
source: NPCs are considered more committed to the neural lineage than NSCs (Oikari et al., 2016) and hence are likely to present higher protein synthesis levels than quiescent NSCs (Baser et al., 2019).
evidence: Cited from Oikari et al., 2016

claim: NPCs are likely to present higher protein synthesis levels than quiescent NSCs.
source: NPCs are considered more committed to the neural lineage than NSCs (Oikari et al., 2016) and hence are likely to present higher protein synthesis levels than quiescent NSCs (Baser et al., 2019).
evidence: Cited from Baser et al., 2019

claim: NPCs maintain the self-renewal and multipotent characteristics of NSCs.
source: Despite their commitment, NPCs maintain the self-renewal and multipotent characteristics of NSCs and, therefore, are widely used to study stem-like properties in vitro.
evidence: General knowledge about NPCs

claim: NPCs cultured for several passages (up to passage 7) presented an increase in the expression of neural markers Pax6 and Sox1.
source: NPCs cultured for several passages (up to passage 7) presented an increase in the expression of neural markers Pax6 and Sox1 and the loss of the pluripotent marker Oct4 (Figure 1C).
evidence: Western blot data shown in Figure 1C

claim: NPCs cultured for several passages (up to passage 7) showed loss of the pluripotent marker Oct4.
source: NPCs cultured for several passages (up to passage 7) presented an increase in the expression of neural markers Pax6 and Sox1 and the loss of the pluripotent marker Oct4 (Figure 1C).
evidence: Western blot data shown in Figure 1C

claim: NPCs treated for 2 hr with forebrain neuron differentiation medium present a significant increase in puromycin incorporation into nascent chains compared to NPCs treated for the same amount of time with medium that keeps them in their undifferentiated state.
source: Our western blotting results show that NPCs treated for 2 hr with forebrain neuron differentiation medium present a significant increase in puromycin incorporation into nascent chains compared to NPCs treated for the same amount of time with medium that keeps them in their undifferentiated state (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B), indicating a differentiation-dependent global increase in protein synthesis.
evidence: Western blot data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B

claim: Early NPC differentiation results in a differentiation-dependent global increase in protein synthesis.
source: Our western blotting results show that NPCs treated for 2 hr with forebrain neuron differentiation medium present a significant increase in puromycin incorporation into nascent chains compared to NPCs treated for the same amount of time with medium that keeps them in their undifferentiated state (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B), indicating a differentiation-dependent global increase in protein synthesis.
evidence: Western blot data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B

claim: eIF3 subunits EIF3A, EIF3B, EIF3D and, to a lesser extent, EIF3G are the four subunits of the complex presenting significant amounts of RNA crosslinks in PAR-CLIP studies.
source: The previous PAR-CLIP studies performed with the eIF3 complex in HEK293T and Jurkat cells identified eIF3 subunits EIF3A, EIF3B, EIF3D and, to a lesser extent, EIF3G as the four subunits of the complex presenting significant amounts of RNA crosslinks (De Silva et al., 2021; Lee et al., 2015).
evidence: Cited from De Silva et al., 2021 and Lee et al., 2015

claim: The top 500 transcripts that crosslink to eIF3 show highly similar sets of mRNAs in undifferentiated and differentiated NPCs (449 in common).
source: Using the STRING database (Szklarczyk et al., 2019) for the top 500 transcripts that crosslink to eIF3, we observed highly similar sets of mRNAs in undifferentiated and differentiated NPCs (449 in common).
evidence: Computational analysis of Quick-irCLIP data

claim: The top 500 transcripts that crosslink to eIF3 show significant enrichment in neurologically-relevant biological processes, such as 'generation of neurons,' 'neuron differentiation,' 'neuron projection development,' and 'axon development'.
source: We observe a significant enrichment in neurologically-relevant biological processes, such as 'generation of neurons,' 'neuron differentiation,' 'neuron projection development,' and 'axon development' (Figure 1I).
evidence: STRING database analysis shown in Figure 1I

claim: Only 12 transcripts are common between NPCs and Jurkat T cells in the top ~200 eIF3-crosslinked transcripts.
source: We found that only 12 are common between NPCs and Jurkat T cells and only eight are common between NPCs and HEK293T, with no common hits between the three cell types (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Comparative analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2

claim: Only eight transcripts are common between NPCs and HEK293T in the top ~200 eIF3-crosslinked transcripts.
source: We found that only 12 are common between NPCs and Jurkat T cells and only eight are common between NPCs and HEK293T, with no common hits between the three cell types (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Comparative analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2

claim: There are no common hits between NPCs, Jurkat T cells, and HEK293T in the top ~200 eIF3-crosslinked transcripts.
source: We found that only 12 are common between NPCs and Jurkat T cells and only eight are common between NPCs and HEK293T, with no common hits between the three cell types (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Comparative analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2

claim: In both differentiated and undifferentiated NPCs, eIF3 predominantly (>90%) crosslinks to mRNAs over other non-coding RNAs such as lncRNAs and snoRNAs.
source: Both in differentiated and undifferentiated NPCs, eIF3 predominantly (>90%) crosslinks to mRNAs over other non-coding RNAs such as lncRNAs and snoRNAs (Figure 1J).
evidence: Quick-irCLIP data shown in Figure 1J

claim: Within mRNA regions, eIF3 primarily interacts with 3'-UTRs and, to a lesser extent, with CDS regions and 5'-UTRs.
source: Within mRNA regions, eIF3 primarily interacts with 3'-UTRs and, to a lesser extent, with CDS regions and 5'-UTRs (Figure 1K).
evidence: Quick-irCLIP data shown in Figure 1K

claim: The Quick-irCLIP experiment in NPCs identified several eIF3 crosslinks located at 5'-UTR regions that were also observed in the previous eIF3 PAR-CLIP experiment performed in HEK293T, such as CCND2 and TUBB mRNAs.
source: Our Quick-irCLIP experiment in NPCs identified several eIF3 crosslinks located at 5'-UTR regions that were also observed in the previous eIF3 PAR-CLIP experiment performed in HEK293T (Lee et al., 2015), such as CCND2 and TUBB mRNAs (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Comparison of Quick-irCLIP data with Lee et al., 2015 shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3

claim: The distinctive 'pan-mRNA' pattern observed in the eIF3 PAR-CLIP performed in Jurkat T cells is not observed in NPCs.
source: The distinctive 'pan-mRNA' pattern observed in the eIF3 PAR-CLIP performed in Jurkat T cells (De Silva et al., 2021) is not observed in NPCs.
evidence: Comparison with De Silva et al., 2021

claim: eIF3 crosslinks are enriched at 3'-UTRs of transcripts encoding neurologically-relevant proteins, such as VIM and NES.
source: Notably, here we observe an enrichment of eIF3 crosslinks at 3'-UTRs of transcripts encoding neurologically-relevant proteins, such as VIM and NES (Figure 1L), as well as highly abundant mRNAs, such as ACTG1 and FTL (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Quick-irCLIP data shown in Figure 1L

claim: eIF3 crosslinks are enriched at 3'-UTRs of highly abundant mRNAs, such as ACTG1 and FTL.
source: Notably, here we observe an enrichment of eIF3 crosslinks at 3'-UTRs of transcripts encoding neurologically-relevant proteins, such as VIM and NES (Figure 1L), as well as highly abundant mRNAs, such as ACTG1 and FTL (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Quick-irCLIP data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4

claim: Similar eIF3 crosslinking levels to transcripts are observed in differentiated and undifferentiated NPCs.
source: Overall, we observe similar eIF3 crosslinking levels to transcripts in differentiated and undifferentiated NPCs (VIM and NES are shown as examples in Figure 1L).
evidence: Quick-irCLIP data shown in Figure 1L

claim: eIF3 crosslinking peaks are observed at the termini of annotated 3'-UTRs, adjacent to the poly(A) tail and where the polyadenylation signal (PAS) is located.
source: In many instances, we observe eIF3 crosslinking peaks at the termini of annotated 3'-UTRs, adjacent to the poly(A) tail and where the polyadenylation signal (PAS; canonical PAS sequence = AAUAAA) is located (Figure 2A, TUBB).
evidence: Quick-irCLIP data shown in Figure 2A

claim: eIF3 crosslinking patterns are observed across multiple regions within 3'-UTRs in addition to ends of annotated 3'-UTRs.
source: However, in addition to ends of annotated 3'-UTRs, we also observe the same type of crosslinking pattern across multiple regions within 3'-UTRs (Figure 1L, VIM).
evidence: Quick-irCLIP data shown in Figure 1L

claim: Most regions within 3'-UTRs where eIF3 crosslinks contain PAS sequences.
source: Looking at the nucleotide sequence of the regions within 3'-UTRs where eIF3 crosslinks, we observe that most of them contain PAS sequences as well (Figure 2A and B, TUBB and APP).
evidence: Sequence analysis of Quick-irCLIP peaks shown in Figure 2A and B

claim: In differentiated NPCs, 58% of the 3'-UTR eIF3 crosslinks map to regions that are extremely enriched in the canonical PAS sequence AAUAAA.
source: Hypergeometric optimization of motif enrichment (HOMER) motif discovery analysis (Heinz et al., 2010) of the eIF3 crosslinks that map to 3'-UTR regions revealed that in differentiated and undifferentiated NPCs 58% and 55% of the 3'-UTR eIF3 crosslinks, respectively, map to regions that are extremely enriched in the canonical PAS sequence AAUAAA (Figure 2C, Supplementary file 2, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: HOMER motif analysis shown in Figure 2C

claim: In undifferentiated NPCs, 55% of the 3'-UTR eIF3 crosslinks map to regions that are extremely enriched in the canonical PAS sequence AAUAAA.
source: Hypergeometric optimization of motif enrichment (HOMER) motif discovery analysis (Heinz et al., 2010) of the eIF3 crosslinks that map to 3'-UTR regions revealed that in differentiated and undifferentiated NPCs 58% and 55% of the 3'-UTR eIF3 crosslinks, respectively, map to regions that are extremely enriched in the canonical PAS sequence AAUAAA (Figure 2C, Supplementary file 2, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: HOMER motif analysis shown in Figure 2C

claim: eIF3 crosslinks near 3'-UTR termini of multiple isoforms, upstream of poly(A) tails in NPCs.
source: Overall, these data indicate eIF3 crosslinks near 3'-UTR termini of multiple isoforms, upstream of poly(A) tails in NPCs.
evidence: Summary of Quick-irCLIP and APA-Seq data

claim: 3'-UTR isoforms play key roles in mRNA localization and expression in different neuronal compartments in neurons.
source: In neurons, 3'-UTR isoforms are known to play key roles in mRNA localization and expression in different neuronal compartments (Taliaferro et al., 2016; Tushev et al., 2018) and alternative polyadenylation is highly prevalent in the nervous system, leading to the expression of multiple mRNA isoforms with different 3'-UTR lengths (Miura et al., 2013).
evidence: Cited from Taliaferro et al., 2016 and Tushev et al., 2018

claim: Alternative polyadenylation is highly prevalent in the nervous system, leading to the expression of multiple mRNA isoforms with different 3'-UTR lengths.
source: In neurons, 3'-UTR isoforms are known to play key roles in mRNA localization and expression in different neuronal compartments (Taliaferro et al., 2016; Tushev et al., 2018) and alternative polyadenylation is highly prevalent in the nervous system, leading to the expression of multiple mRNA isoforms with different 3'-UTR lengths (Miura et al., 2013).
evidence: Cited from Miura et al., 2013

claim: The eIF3 peaks located in 3'-UTRs map to the same location as APA peaks.
source: Comparing our Quick-irCLIP and APA-Seq experiments, we observe that the eIF3 peaks located in 3'-UTRs map to the same location as APA peaks, indicating that the predominant eIF3 crosslinking peaks in 3'-UTRs identified by Quick-irCLIP localize to 3'-UTR termini, adjacent to the poly(A) tail.
evidence: Comparison of Quick-irCLIP and APA-Seq data

claim: The predominant eIF3 crosslinking peaks in 3'-UTRs identified by Quick-irCLIP localize to 3'-UTR termini, adjacent to the poly(A) tail.
source: Comparing our Quick-irCLIP and APA-Seq experiments, we observe that the eIF3 peaks located in 3'-UTRs map to the same location as APA peaks, indicating that the predominant eIF3 crosslinking peaks in 3'-UTRs identified by Quick-irCLIP localize to 3'-UTR termini, adjacent to the poly(A) tail.
evidence: Comparison of Quick-irCLIP and APA-Seq data

claim: The eIF3 crosslinking peaks located in the 3'-UTR of the MAP1B mRNA correspond to APA-Seq peaks.
source: For instance, the eIF3 crosslinking peaks located in the 3'-UTR of the MAP1B mRNA correspond to APA-Seq peaks (Figure 2D).
evidence: Quick-irCLIP and APA-Seq data shown in Figure 2D

claim: S100B encodes for a calcium-binding protein highly expressed in brain cells and is commonly used as a glial marker.
source: As another example, our irCLIP experiment shows that eIF3 crosslinks to both the 5'- and 3'-UTRs of the S100B mRNA, which encodes for a calcium-binding protein highly expressed in brain cells and that is commonly used as a glial marker (Brockes et al., 1979; Ferri et al., 1982; Ludwin et al., 1976).
evidence: Cited from Brockes et al., 1979; Ferri et al., 1982; Ludwin et al., 1976

claim: eIF3 crosslinks to both the 5'- and 3'-UTRs of the S100B mRNA.
source: As another example, our irCLIP experiment shows that eIF3 crosslinks to both the 5'- and 3'-UTRs of the S100B mRNA, which encodes for a calcium-binding protein highly expressed in brain cells and that is commonly used as a glial marker (Brockes et al., 1979; Ferri et al., 1982; Ludwin et al., 1976).
evidence: Quick-irCLIP data

claim: Within S100B's 3'-UTR, there are 2 major eIF3 crosslinking peaks at the 3'-UTR termini of 2 distinct S100B mRNA isoforms expressed in NPCs.
source: Within S100B's 3'-UTR, we observe 2 major eIF3 crosslinking peaks at the 3'-UTR termini of 2 distinct S100B mRNA isoforms expressed in NPCs (Figure 2D).
evidence: Quick-irCLIP and APA-Seq data shown in Figure 2D

claim: eIF3 exhibits different crosslinking levels to the 3'-UTR termini of various 3'-UTR isoforms that are similarly expressed.
source: Interestingly, we found that eIF3 exhibits different crosslinking levels to the 3'-UTR termini of various 3'-UTR isoforms that are similarly expressed.
evidence: Comparison of Quick-irCLIP and APA-Seq data

claim: eIF3 preferentially crosslinks to the distal 3'-UTR isoform rather than the proximal 3'-UTR isoform of S100B.
source: For instance, our APA-Seq data reveals two major S100B mRNAs with similar expression levels. However, eIF3 preferentially crosslinks to the distal 3'-UTR isoform rather than the proximal 3'-UTR isoform (Figure 2D).
evidence: Quick-irCLIP and APA-Seq data shown in Figure 2D

claim: In the case of APP, eIF3 predominantly binds to the 3'-UTR terminus of the proximal isoform.
source: Conversely, in the case of APP, which also expresses 2 major mRNA isoforms, eIF3 predominantly binds to the 3'-UTR terminus of the proximal isoform.
evidence: Quick-irCLIP and APA-Seq data

claim: In TUBB mRNA, the extent of eIF3 crosslinking correlates with mRNA isoform expression.
source: Finally, similar to the case of MAP1B mRNA, in TUBB mRNA the extent of eIF3 crosslinking correlates with mRNA isoform expression, indicating that eIF3 binds to both major TUBB mRNA isoforms to a similar extent (Figure 2D).
evidence: Quick-irCLIP and APA-Seq data shown in Figure 2D

claim: eIF3 binds to both major TUBB mRNA isoforms to a similar extent.
source: Finally, similar to the case of MAP1B mRNA, in TUBB mRNA the extent of eIF3 crosslinking correlates with mRNA isoform expression, indicating that eIF3 binds to both major TUBB mRNA isoforms to a similar extent (Figure 2D).
evidence: Quick-irCLIP and APA-Seq data shown in Figure 2D

claim: The eIF3 crosslinking events that occur in 3'-UTRs often occur at 3'-UTR termini of multiple mRNA isoforms, upstream of poly(A) tails.
source: Overall, these results show that the eIF3 crosslinking events that we observe in 3'-UTRs often occur at 3'-UTR termini of multiple mRNA isoforms, upstream of poly(A) tails.
evidence: Summary of Quick-irCLIP and APA-Seq data

claim: eIF3 interacts with the 3'-UTR termini of mRNAs expressed in both differentiated and undifferentiated NPCs.
source: Our Quick-irCLIP experiment showed that eIF3 interacts with the 3'-UTR termini of mRNAs expressed in both differentiated and undifferentiated NPCs.
evidence: Quick-irCLIP data

claim: eIF3 interacts with the mRNA encoding the transcription regulator ID2 only upon NPC differentiation.
source: Interestingly, eIF3 interacts with the mRNA encoding the transcription regulator ID2 only upon NPC differentiation (Figure 3A).
evidence: Quick-irCLIP data shown in Figure 3A

claim: ID2 is involved in migrating NPC differentiation into olfactory dopaminergic neurons.
source: ID2 is involved in migrating NPC differentiation into olfactory dopaminergic neurons (Havrda et al., 2008).
evidence: Cited from Havrda et al., 2008

claim: eIF3 interactions with 3'-UTR termini are involved with active translation levels for a given transcript.
source: Therefore, it is possible that the observed eIF3 engagement at its 3'-UTR terminus in differentiated NPCs is due to ID2's mRNA translation activation upon differentiation. This would suggest that eIF3 interactions with 3'-UTR termini are involved with active translation levels for a given transcript.
evidence: Inference from ID2 data

claim: For most mRNAs (n=6300 of a total of 8427, i.e. ∼75%), translation efficiency levels remain unchanged upon NPC differentiation.
source: Our ribosome profiling experiment indicates that for most mRNAs (n=6300 of a total of 8427, i.e. ∼75%), translation efficiency levels (RPF counts/mRNA counts) remain unchanged upon NPC differentiation (Figure 3B, Supplementary file 4,).
evidence: Ribosome profiling data shown in Figure 3B

claim: ID2 is one of the transcripts with the highest increase in both RPFs and mRNA counts upon NPC differentiation.
source: ID2 is one of the transcripts with the highest increase in both RPFs and mRNA counts upon NPC differentiation (Figure 3B).
evidence: Ribosome profiling data shown in Figure 3B

claim: NPC differentiation results in a >fivefold RPF count increase for ID2.
source: Specifically, we observe a >fivefold RPF count increase upon NPC differentiation (Figure 3C), indicating a significant burst in ID2 mRNA translation activity.
evidence: Ribosome profiling data shown in Figure 3C

claim: NPC differentiation results in a significant increase in ID2 mRNA transcript levels (~15 fold).
source: However, we also observe that NPC differentiation results in a significant increase in ID2 mRNA transcript levels (~15 fold, Figure 3C).
evidence: mRNA-Seq data shown in Figure 3C

claim: Western blots of ID2 and SLC38A2 (SNAT2) are in agreement with the ribosome profiling data showing increased RPFs on their mRNAs in differentiated vs. undifferentiated NPCs.
source: Western blots of ID2 and a second protein SLC38A2 (SNAT2) with increased RPFs on its mRNA in differentiated vs. undifferentiated NPCs are in agreement with the ribosome profiling data (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Western blot data shown in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 3

claim: The observed stepwise increase in ID2 mRNA levels and translation is well corroborated by the observed increase in eIF3 crosslinking to ID2 mRNA's 3'-UTR termini.
source: Notably, this observed stepwise increase in ID2 mRNA levels and translation is well corroborated by our observed increase in eIF3 crosslinking to ID2 mRNA's 3'-UTR termini, suggesting a connection for eIF3 in maintaining and promoting ID2 translation upon differentiation beyond the 5'-UTR.
evidence: Integration of Quick-irCLIP and ribosome profiling data

claim: The most actively translated transcripts, such as EEF1A and ACTB, present significant eIF3 peaks at their 3'-UTR termini.
source: We next looked at the most actively translated transcripts in NPCs by sorting the ribosome profiling hits based on their amount of RPFs. We noticed that the most actively translated transcripts, such as EEF1A and ACTB, also present significant eIF3 peaks at their 3'-UTR termini (Figure 3E).
evidence: Quick-irCLIP and ribosome profiling data shown in Figure 3E

claim: eIF3 interacts with 3'-UTR ends of mRNAs being actively translated.
source: Together with the ID2 mRNA results, these data suggest that eIF3 interacts with 3'-UTR ends of mRNAs being actively translated.
evidence: Integration of Quick-irCLIP and ribosome profiling data

claim: Genes which had an increase in 3'-UTR irCLIP crosslinking tended to have an increase in ribosome occupancy in both undifferentiated and differentiated NPCs.
source: Indeed, regardless of whether we examined undifferentiated or differentiated NPCs, we found genes which had an increase in 3'-UTR irCLIP crosslinking tended to have an increase in ribosome occupancy (Figure 3F, Figure 3—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: DESeq2 analysis shown in Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 4A

claim: The increase in 3'-UTR irCLIP crosslinking correlated less well with increases in translational efficiency.
source: By contrast, the increase in 3'-UTR irCLIP crosslinking correlated less well with increases in translational efficiency (Figure 3G, Figure 3—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: DESeq2 analysis shown in Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplement 4B

claim: In both undifferentiated and differentiated NPCs, there is a global increase in eIF3 engagement at 3'-UTR termini that correlates with an overall increase in protein synthesis.
source: Overall, our ribosome profiling data combined with our eIF3 irCLIP data suggest that, in both undifferentiated and differentiated NPCs, there is a global increase in eIF3 engagement at 3'-UTR termini that correlates with an overall increase in protein synthesis.
evidence: Integration of ribosome profiling and Quick-irCLIP data

claim: Canonical histone mRNAs are the only known cellular non-polyadenylated mRNAs in eukaryotes due to their cell-cycle dependency and their need to be degraded rapidly.
source: Canonical histone mRNAs are the only known cellular non-polyadenylated mRNAs in eukaryotes due to their cell-cycle dependency and their need to be degraded rapidly.
evidence: General knowledge about histone mRNAs

claim: Several variant histone mRNAs are not cell-cycle dependent and are polyadenylated.
source: On the other hand, several variant histone mRNAs are not cell-cycle dependent and are polyadenylated.
evidence: General knowledge about variant histone mRNAs

claim: In non-polyadenylated canonical histone mRNAs (H2AC11, H3C1, and H4-16), there are no traces of eIF3 crosslinking at 3'-UTR termini nor APA events.
source: In non-polyadenylated canonical histone mRNAs (H2AC11, H3C1, and H4-16), we see no traces of eIF3 crosslinking at 3'-UTR termini nor APA events, as expected (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Quick-irCLIP and APA-Seq data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A

claim: For the variant polyadenylated histone mRNAs (H3-3B and H2AZ1), eIF3 crosslinks localize with APA-Seq peaks.
source: However, for the variant polyadenylated histone mRNAs (H3-3B and H2AZ1), we observe eIF3 crosslinks that localize with APA-Seq peaks (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Quick-irCLIP and APA-Seq data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A

claim: eIF3 crosslinking to the 3'-UTR termini had a positive association with polyadenylation.
source: We also carried out a global comparison of the eIF3 Quick-irCLIP and APA-Seq crosslinking peaks, and observed that eIF3 crosslinking to the 3'-UTR termini had a positive association with polyadenylation (Methods).
evidence: Statistical analysis of Quick-irCLIP and APA-Seq data

claim: eIF3 only interacts with 3'-UTR termini of mRNAs that are polyadenylated.
source: These data indicate that eIF3 only interacts with 3'-UTR termini of mRNAs that are polyadenylated, and thus should be in close proximity to the poly(A) tail.
evidence: Analysis of histone mRNAs and global comparison of Quick-irCLIP and APA-Seq data

claim: eIF3 has been reported to interact with the poly(A)-binding protein interacting protein 1 (PAIP1) in HeLa cells through the EIF3G subunit to promote closed loop formation.
source: eIF3 has been reported to interact with the poly(A)-binding protein interacting protein 1 (PAIP1) in HeLa cells through the EIF3G subunit to promote closed loop formation (Martineau et al., 2008).
evidence: Cited from Martineau et al., 2008

claim: Despite eIF3 being in close proximity to the location of the PABPs, PAIP1 and PABPC1 do not elute with eIF3 in immunoprecipitation from UV-crosslinked undifferentiated NPCs.
source: Our results indicate that despite eIF3 being in close proximity to the location of the PABPs, these do not elute with it (Figure 4B).
evidence: Immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4B

claim: Immunoprecipitation of eIF3 complexes from UV-crosslinked HEK293T gave the same results as NPCs regarding PAIP1 and PABPC1 not eluting with eIF3.
source: Immunoprecipitation of eIF3 complexes from UV-crosslinked HEK293T gave the same results (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B

claim: Even when protein-protein transient interactions are covalently linked by DSP treatment, PABPC1 and PAIP1 do not elute with eIF3 in NPCs.
source: Our results show that even when protein-protein transient interactions are covalently linked by DSP treatment, PABPC1 and PAIP1 do not elute with eIF3 in NPCs (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: DSP-treated immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C

claim: DSP-treated immunoprecipitation experiments performed in HEK293T gave the same results as NPCs regarding PABPC1 and PAIP1 not eluting with eIF3.
source: The same experiments performed in HEK293T gave the same results (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: DSP-treated immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C

claim: eIF3 engagement with 3'-UTR termini in highly translated transcripts requires polyadenylation but is independent of interactions with poly(A)-binding proteins.
source: Overall, these results suggest that eIF3 engagement with 3'-UTR termini in highly translated transcripts requires polyadenylation but is independent of interactions with poly(A)-binding proteins.
evidence: Summary of histone mRNA analysis and immunoprecipitation experiments

claim: eIF3 predominantly crosslinks to 3'-UTRs in NPCs.
source: Our Quick-irCLIP experiment shows that eIF3 predominantly crosslinks to 3'-UTRs in NPCs.
evidence: Quick-irCLIP data

claim: eIF3 3'-UTR crosslinks map to 3'-UTR termini of multiple mRNA isoforms, adjacent to poly(A) tails and where the polyadenylation signal is located.
source: By performing APA-Seq, we discovered that these eIF3 3'-UTR crosslinks map to 3'-UTR termini of multiple mRNA isoforms, adjacent to poly(A) tails and where the polyadenylation signal is located.
evidence: APA-Seq data

claim: eIF3 irCLIP peaks within mRNA coding regions colocalize with APA-Seq peaks, indicating that different protein isoforms are expressed in NPCs.
source: Interestingly, we have also identified eIF3 irCLIP peaks within mRNA coding regions such as in NES mRNA (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A) that colocalize with APA-Seq peaks, indicating that different nestin protein isoforms are expressed in NPCs.
evidence: Quick-irCLIP and APA-Seq data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A

claim: Early NPC differentiation results in eIF3 engagement with the 3'-UTR terminus of the mRNA encoding the transcription regulator ID2.
source: Here, we also observe that early NPC differentiation results in eIF3 engagement with the 3'-UTR terminus of the mRNA encoding the transcription regulator ID2.
evidence: Quick-irCLIP data

claim: The increase in eIF3 engagement on ID2 mRNA is correlated with an increase in the levels of active transcription and translation of ID2.
source: By ribosome profiling, we determined that this increase in eIF3 engagement on ID2 mRNA is correlated with an increase in the levels of active transcription and translation of ID2 (Figure 3).
evidence: Ribosome profiling data shown in Figure 3

claim: At a global level, in both undifferentiated and differentiated NPCs, mRNAs with higher levels of eIF3 crosslinks to 3'-UTRs exhibit higher levels of active translation.
source: At a global level, we also observe in both undifferentiated and differentiated NPCs mRNAs with higher levels of eIF3 crosslinks to 3'-UTRs exhibit higher levels of active translation (Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 4), suggesting that these two phenomena are correlated.

claim: eIF3's presence at the very end of 3'-UTRs of actively translated mRNAs supports the mRNA circularization model.
source: eIF3 is an initiation factor that is usually associated with 5'-UTRs, where it organizes interactions between other initiation factors and the 40 S ribosomal subunit during translation initiation. Its presence at the very end of 3'-UTRs of actively translated mRNAs supports the mRNA circularization model, where the 5' and 3' ends of highly translated mRNAs are proposed to be brought in close proximity to each other by the interactions of multiple proteins that bridge 5'-UTRs with 3'-UTRs (Wells et al., 1998).
evidence: Inference from Quick-irCLIP data and cited from Wells et al., 1998
